Today in brief

latin-america
  • Houthi attacks in the Strait of Hormuz raise alarm in Latin American oil importers, fearing supply disruptions and higher prices.
  • Trump announced plans to lift tariffs on €450 million of Irish whiskey, a move praised by Latin American distributors seeking cheaper European spirits.
europe
  • Kersti Kaljulaid warns that global air‑defence supplies fall short of Ukraine’s needs, urging faster production and delivery.
  • Sweden’s parliamentary vote shows the social‑democratic left leading, while the far‑right loses ground in a tight race.
  • NATO allies discuss tougher measures against Russia, calling for more aggressive drills to pressure Putin’s troops out of Ukraine.
  • Former Anthropic researcher tells BBC AI poses real dangers, saying employees feel terrified by unchecked development.
oceania
  • Australian man and his two children were found dead in Bali in a suspected double‑murder‑suicide, prompting an Australian police investigation.
  • Critics say the new GST deal will lower living standards across Australia, except for Queensland, which may see modest gains.
other
  • Les arbitres admettent une « erreur de jugement » après que Manchester City a profité d’une faute VAR contre United.
  • Suite aux troubles sur Krk et à Rijeka, des amendes sévères sont imposées, les conducteurs risquant jusqu’à 2 650 €.
  • Le candidat au poste de gouverneur du Wisconsin a survécu à un atterrissage d’urgence sur le lac après que son avion a fait naufrage.
middle-east
  • Iran postponed its meeting with Gulf states in Oman after several regional countries requested a delay, citing diplomatic sensitivities.
  • The West shows inconsistent reactions, condemning Iran’s regional moves while largely ignoring the Houthi militia’s escalating attacks.
  • Saudi Civil Defense issued early warnings for potential attacks on four major cities, urging residents to stay alert.
  • Oman’s energy minister announced the Strait of Hormuz will reopen soon, expecting only a short‑term disruption.
asia
  • Oil prices jumped 3% as Middle East tensions escalated, pressuring Asian importers and boosting regional market volatility.
  • Houthis advanced toward the Bab el‑Mandeb strait, prompting Saudi retaliatory strikes and raising concerns for shipping lanes vital to Asian trade.
  • Despite winning a major tournament, Indian female athletes have yet to receive their medals from the National Association of Kinetic Volleyball Initiatives.
north-america
  • Trump announced he will lift the U.S. tariff on Irish whiskey after receiving repeated complaints.
  • Defence Minister departed for China following an invitation from his Chinese counterpart to discuss bilateral security issues.
  • The Kennedy Center warned it may close as early as Tuesday due to looming bankruptcy, according to internal documents.
africa
  • Inflation surged again across sub‑Saharan Africa, with Nigeria and Kenya reporting year‑on‑year price rises above 20%.
  • Youth activists from South Africa’s List 51 rallied in Johannesburg, urging citizens to join their campaign for land reform and job creation.
  • Security forces evacuated dozens of displaced families from a school in Al‑Tawahi, Sudan, after coastal flooding forced them to flee.
